entities.summary:
Wired is an American technology magazine that has significantly shaped discourse around technology, culture, and innovation since its inception in 1993. Headquartered in San Francisco, California, Wired was co-founded by Louis Rossetto and Jane Metcalfe, who envisioned a publication that would not only report on technological advancements but also explore their implications for society. This vision allowed Wired to play a pivotal role in the cultural landscape of the late 20th and early 21st centuries, positioning itself at the intersection of technology and liberal arts. By focusing on how technology influences various aspects of human life, Wired has become a vital source for understanding the complexities of contemporary digital culture.

The magazine's debut issue in March 1993 featured an article about the World Wide Web, a platform that was just beginning to gain traction. This early coverage was indicative of Wired's forward-thinking approach, as it not only reported on technological innovations but also critiqued and contextualized them. Over the years, Wired has published groundbreaking articles on topics ranging from artificial intelligence to cybersecurity, often featuring influential voices like Kevin Kelly and Jaron Lanier. Its commitment to in-depth reporting has resulted in numerous accolades, including National Magazine Awards, solidifying its reputation as a leading voice in technology journalism.
